r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: THE BLOCK IS CLOSED. Round 1 failed this item because one clause asserted a mechanism ("the archive gate requires the lease to cover every journaled action") that did not exist at the site it named, inside a sentence advertising itself as measured. Every claim in the repaired paragraph is now grounded, each named to its file/symbol/measurement. (1) "with your own lease held, binding a second checklist is REFUSED" -- reproduced by me in a FRESH PROCESS (door_probe.py case bound-then-rebind), isError=True, and spine_status afterwards still shows the first spine, so the refusal is total. (2) The quoted fragment -- the probe EXTRACTS the quote from the specs themselves via tomllib and matches each half against the live refusal, so it compares shipped text to the door rather than to a copy I retyped: both halves present, including the rework's `release`->`Release` capitalisation fix. VERBATIM_OK=True. (3) "your role skill holds the lease open until your last action" -- skills/{reviewer,implementer}/SKILL.md:17, "only then `release` the engine session lease as your very last action"; repo and installed copies identical. (4) "the lease must cover every journaled action" -- verbatim on those same lines. (5) "releasing it early fails the terminal provenance check" -- those same lines name that check; the term is inherited vocabulary in 6 skill files, invented nowhere. (6) "Dispatched without a spine of your own you arrive holding no lease" -- run_crew._crew_door_env(spine=None) under a CLEAN ambient env returns SPINE_PARENT only, no SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION; my own dispatch environment is the live case (0 of those two vars set). (7) "nothing to release, and the escape never arises" -- probe case unbound-then-bind: spine_status REFUSES "no spine is bound to this door", then spine_bind SUCCEEDS with no release step, returning SPINE_SESSION derived from the spine's own work_id. POSITIVE CONTROL, because an absence over an unexercised path reads like a passing check: case released-then-rebind runs the IDENTICAL bind after releasing and SUCCEEDS, so the refusal is conditioned on holding your own lease and nothing else -- the reason the prose gives. DURABILITY, which the handoff did not ask for: this lane merges last and lane E already rewrote the door on main, so I re-ran the whole probe against main's post-cf6cdaa2 door -- the refusal and both quote halves survive there too, so the merge will not falsify the quote.

(h) decision:one-spine-per-process-stands is real and cited where the behaviour lives (scripts/mcp_spine_server.py, docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md). r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No divergence that blocks this gate; two things the Commander should carry. (1) SCOPING VERDICT, the addendum's item 2: both halves are true of their reader and neither reader is left with the other's rule. Reader A (holds its own lease) gets the refusal plus the role-skill rule that bars the release-to-escape; measured true. Reader B (dispatched with no spine) gets "you arrive holding no lease -- nothing to release, and the escape never arises"; measured true, and I am the live case. The one subtlety, which I judged an observation rather than a finding: reader B stops being lease-less the moment it binds and claims its own plan, and from then on sentence 2 governs it -- which is also true of it, since the role-skill rule is addressed to any reviewer. The paragraph does not leave B exempt, because the closing sentence is unconditional -- "the door reaches the spine you hold a lease on, and you hold a lease on exactly one" -- and it forecloses the misreading. "Arrive" carries the temporal scoping honestly. (2) THE DIVERGENCE WORTH THE COMMANDER'S ATTENTION, and it is out of scope rather than wrong: the door vocabulary landed on the specs surface ONLY. skills/reviewer/templates/REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json and skills/implementer/templates/IMPLEMENTER_PLAN.template.json contain ZERO occurrences of "door" anywhere in the file, and nothing links the two surfaces -- generate_spine.py emits to a --out path, no test asserts the compiled spec equals the shipped template, and the specs' own header comment claims only that intent "matches" the template. So a crew that instantiates its checklist FROM THE TEMPLATE -- which is what the role SKILL.md directs an unbound crew to do, and what I did to build this very survey -- never receives the second-checklist rule the specs now state. The weaker form of it survives in SKILL.md prose ("Do not author a survey of your own when a spine is already bound"); the measured reason does not. Flagged as a triage candidate, NO issue filed. skills/** is fenced from this lane, so this could not have been fixed here. (3) Round 1's tc1 stands unclosed and the implementer says so explicitly: "terminal provenance check" is binding role doctrine whose only mechanical enforcement is evals/euler-*/checks/spine_completed.py::journal_consistent, which no live path calls. The repaired clause is careful about this -- it attributes the rule to "your role skill" rather than to a gate -- so it does not re-commit round 1's error, but the gap is still real upstream.

r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from <work-id> alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.
